decisions.reason: As a highly specialized particle-therapy phantom it is a niche and still very new offer with some market-access delay, but it builds strongly on the firm's radiotherapy measurement know-how so we would continue learning from the launch rather than exit quickly.

A small volume ionization chamber is close to the firm's core dosimetry capabilities, so early market feedback can be absorbed and used for refinement, making withdrawal within a year relatively unlikely.

Although another small volume ionization chamber may create some overlap in the portfolio, it is still strongly related to existing knowledge and therefore more likely to be improved or repositioned than dropped outright.
A standard clinical ionization chamber sits at the center of the firm's established competence base and likely serves routine demand, so there is little reason to remove it after only one year.
An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry is an adjacent, technically familiar product where the firm can readily interpret user feedback and iterate, supporting continuation.
A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional product format in the firm's domain, and its strong fit with existing R&D and application knowledge argues for keeping it on the market.
